unit.title: Coordinate the installation of electrical cable and fixture

theory1.instructions: Answer all 45 questions. Each question has one best answer: choose it. Each question is worth 1 mark. Time allowed: 2 hours 30 minutes. Your answers are saved as you go.

questions.stem: What does a cable schedule for a project list?
options: The prices each supplier charged for cable last year
Each cable's reference, size, type, route, length and ends
The names of the workers who will pull each of the cables
The colours that the client wants for the faceplates

questions.stem: A job needs runs of 85 m, 70 m and 60 m of the same cable. The supplier sells 100 m and 250 m drums. Which order is best?
options: One 250 m drum, so each run is one length with no joints
Two 100 m drums, and join the cable where a run is short
Short coils from the hardware store, as they are easier
200 m in total, since a little cable will always stretch

questions.stem: How should a heavy cable drum be moved a short distance over level ground?
options: Rolled in any direction, as long as it moves slowly
Lifted by hand by two people holding the flanges
Rolled in the direction of the arrow on the drum
Dropped flat off the truck and dragged with a rope

questions.stem: Cable is to be paid out from a drum for a long pull. Which set-up is right?
options: Lying flat on the ground so the cable comes off the top
Standing on its edge against a wall, with no support
Held upright by a worker who spins it round by hand
On a spindle and stands, so it turns under control

questions.stem: Why must the pulling force on a long cable be kept below the maker's limit?
options: So that the colour of the outer sheath does not fade
So that the drum does not run out of cable too soon
Too much force stretches and damages the conductors
So the pull takes longer and the crew can take a rest

questions.stem: On a long cable pull through several floors, how should the crew keep in contact?
options: Shout loudly whenever anyone sees a problem
Each person decides alone when to pull or stop
Pull as fast as they can so the job ends sooner
Radios or agreed signals, with one person in charge

questions.stem: At a sharp corner during a pull, what should be used to stop the cable being bent too tightly?
options: A worker's knee pressed hard against the cable
A cable roller or corner sheave
A piece of timber nailed across the corner
Nothing, since the cable will bend by itself

questions.stem: What is a cable pulling sock (stocking) used for?
options: Gripping a cable end so a rope or winch can pull it
Keeping the cable warm before it is installed
Covering a joint so that water cannot get in
Marking the cable so that it can be found later

questions.stem: Why is the end of a cable sealed after a length has been cut from the drum?
options: To stop anyone using the cable without asking
To show where the next cut on the drum must be
To make the drum easier to roll across the site
To keep out moisture and dirt until it is used

questions.stem: Why should each cable be labelled at both ends as it is pulled in?
options: So the client can see how much cable was used
So each end can be matched to the schedule
So the cable maker can be traced if it fails
So the cables look neat from the ceiling below

questions.stem: Copper cable left on site overnight is often stolen. What is the best way to protect it?
options: Have it delivered close to need, and lock it in a store
Leave it on the drum by the gate where the guard can see
Pull it all in on the first day, even before it is needed
Paint the drums a bright colour so thieves will not want it

questions.stem: A fire alarm cable and a lighting cable must run along the same corridor. What should the coordinator check?
options: That both are in the same conduit to save money
That the fire alarm cable is tied to the lighting one
That they are kept apart as the specification says
That the fire alarm cable is the cheapest on offer

questions.stem: Why is fire-resistant cable used for emergency lighting and fire alarm circuits?
options: So the circuit keeps working for a time in a fire
So the cable costs less than ordinary PVC cable
So the circuit does not need a protective device
So the lamps can be brighter than ordinary ones

questions.stem: What does a luminaire (fixture) schedule tell the installer?
options: The time each worker must start and finish each day
The supplier's bank account details for payment
The type, lamp, mounting and place of each fitting
The colour of the walls in each room of the building

questions.stem: Why must a ceiling fan be hung from a box or bracket rated for fans?
options: Fan-rated boxes come with the speed control fitted
Ordinary boxes are too small to take the fan's cable
A fan-rated box makes the fan run more quietly
A fan's weight and shaking can pull out a normal box

questions.stem: A heavy chandelier is to be hung in a hotel lobby. What should the coordinator check first?
options: That its lamps are the brightest that can be bought
Its weight, and that the fixing point can hold it
That it is the same style as the lobby's chairs
That it can be wired to any spare outlet circuit

questions.stem: Recessed downlights are going into a suspended ceiling. With whom must the electrical coordinator agree their layout and cut-outs?
options: The painting contractor
The ceiling installer
The plumbing contractor
The landscaping crew

questions.stem: Why must recessed light fittings be rated for contact with ceiling insulation, or be kept clear of it?
options: Covered fittings can overheat and start a fire
Insulation makes the lamps shine more dimly
Insulation stops the light switch from working
Covered fittings use more electricity each month

questions.stem: Which light fitting is right for a hotel's outdoor pool deck?
options: An indoor fitting with a plastic bag over it
Any fitting, as long as it is high up on a wall
One with an IP rating suited to rain and splashes
A fitting with no cover, so that heat can escape

questions.stem: Where does the installer find the mounting heights of switches and outlets for a project?
options: From the height of the tallest member of the crew
From whatever heights were used on the last job
From the pictures in a supplier's catalogue
From the specification and the drawings

questions.stem: Dimmable LED lamps flicker on a newly fitted dimmer. What is the most likely cause?
options: The lamps are too bright for the size of the room
The circuit's breaker is rated too high for them
The dimmer is not compatible with those LEDs
The switch box was fixed too low on the wall

questions.stem: After emergency light fittings are installed, a competent person cuts their normal supply to test them. What should happen?
options: They go out at once to save their batteries
The normal lights in the room get brighter
The main breaker trips to warn the occupants
They light and stay on for their rated time

questions.stem: An outdoor security light should come on only at night. Which device does this?
options: A thermostat
A photocell (light sensor)
A time-delay fuse
A float switch

questions.stem: Fittings are being installed in a hotel while painters are still working. What should the coordinator arrange?
options: Cover the fittings, and agree the order of work
Ask the painters to paint carefully around them
Leave them uncovered so the client sees progress
Take the lamps out and leave the fittings open

questions.stem: Why are fixtures and accessories usually fitted after the plastering and painting are done?
options: The cables are not pulled in until after painting
Fitting them is cheaper when done during the rain
The inspector only visits after painting is done
So they are not damaged or covered in plaster

questions.stem: When connecting a light fitting, what should be done with the circuit's protective conductor?
options: Cut it off short if the fitting is all plastic
Connect it to the earth terminal, or in a connector
Join it to the neutral to make a better return path
Leave it loose and bare inside the ceiling rose

questions.stem: Pendant fittings that use hot-running lamps need what kind of flexible cord?
options: Heat-resistant flex suited to the temperature
Any thin flex, as long as it is a bright colour
Bare copper wires twisted together for strength
Speaker cable, because it is easy to get hold of

questions.stem: When installing a 220 V water heater, where should its double-pole isolator be?
options: Inside the heater, behind its metal cover
In a cupboard in another room, out of sight
Within reach and in sight of the heater
At the main board only, with nothing local

questions.stem: A trainee has fitted ten outlets, but several faceplates are not level. What should the coordinator do?
options: Show the method again and have them refix the plates
Refix them himself later without telling the trainee
Leave them, as the client may not notice them at all
Take the trainee off outlets for the rest of the job

questions.stem: Cables above a suspended ceiling are found lying on the ceiling tiles. What should be done?
options: Leave them, since the tiles will support them
Tape them to the hangers of the ceiling grid
Support them on proper clips, tray or hangers
Push them further away from the access panel

questions.stem: During a pull, a cable's sheath is scraped through to the insulation. What should the coordinator do?
options: Wrap the damage with tape and carry on with the pull
Leave it, because the inner insulation is not broken
Turn the cable so the damaged side faces the wall
Stop, assess it, and replace or repair as specified

questions.stem: What should be done with leftover cable at the end of a job?
options: Leave it up in the ceiling space for future use
Return it to stores, record it, recycle the scrap
Burn the insulation off so the copper can be sold
Put it out with the client's household rubbish

questions.stem: A lighting circuit's route on the drawing is 64 m. Allowing 15% extra for drops and terminations, how much cable is needed?
options: About 66 m
About 74 m
About 79 m
About 96 m

questions.stem: An electrician fits 6 downlights an hour. How long will 90 downlights take one person?
options: 15 hours
9 hours
54 hours
12 hours

questions.stem: When may a light fitting rest on a suspended ceiling grid?
options: Always, because the grid can hold any weight
Only when it is held on with adhesive tape
Only as the makers allow, with extra hangers
Only if the fitting has no glass parts in it

questions.stem: After the dead tests pass, who switches on new lighting and outlet circuits for the function test?
options: The newest trainee, to give him some experience
The client, as it is now their own building
Any member of the crew who is near the board
A competent person, following the procedure

questions.stem: What is a snag list at the end of an installation?
options: A list of the crew's complaints about the job
A list of the tools lost during the installation
A list of defects and unfinished items to correct
A list of the members of the client's family

questions.stem: Which documents about the fixtures should go to the client at handover?
options: The crew's timesheets for each week of the job
The supplier's invoices, showing the prices paid
The coordinator's own work phone bill
The makers' instructions, warranties and schedules

questions.stem: A bathroom exhaust fan is to be fitted close to a shower. What must the coordinator check?
options: That its colour matches the bathroom's tiles
That it suits that wet zone and is RCD-protected
That it plugs into the nearest outlet on a lead
That its switch is placed inside the shower

questions.stem: Two crews need the same mobile scaffold on the same morning. What should the coordinator do?
options: Plan the order so each crew has it at set times
Let the crew that arrives first keep it all day
Tell one crew to use ladders standing on tables
Cancel both jobs until a second one is bought

questions.stem: A box of light fittings arrives with cracked diffusers. What should the coordinator do?
options: Fit them anyway, since the cracks are only small
Glue the cracks and fit them on the top floor
Throw them out and reorder without telling anyone
Note it on the delivery note and ask for new ones

questions.stem: An LED strip light is rated 24 V DC. What must it be fed from?
options: A 220 V outlet, connected directly
A suitable 24 V DC driver or power supply
A dimmer switch on its own, with no driver
The 110 V supply to a nearby water heater

questions.stem: When terminating at an outlet, why should the conductors be folded neatly into the box?
options: So the plate fits with no strain on the terminals
So the box can hold spare cable for later use
So the conductors touch for a better earth path
So the box stays cool while the outlet is in use

questions.stem: A floodlight is to be fixed on a pole in a car park in Ocho Rios. Which check matters most for strong winds?
options: That its lamp is the brightest one on sale
That the cable feeding it is the cheapest type
That the bracket and pole are rated for its wind load
That the floodlight is pointed toward the sea

questions.stem: At the end of each week, how should the coordinator report progress on cables and fixtures?
options: By telling the client nothing until the very end
By guessing a percentage done from memory alone
Against the schedules: done, left to do, problems
By sending photos of the crew at their lunch

theory2.instructions: Section A has 15 short answers (2 marks each). Section B has 10 essay questions (5 marks each): answer each in full sentences. Time allowed: 3 hours 35 minutes. Your answers are saved as you go.

shortAnswers.stem: What machine, with a rope and a drum or capstan, is used to pull long, heavy cables mechanically?
In which unit is the total light output of a lamp given?
What is the stage of work called when fittings and accessories are fixed and connected, after plastering?
In an IP rating, what does IP stand for?
Each hotel room needs 3 fittings at J$4 500 each. What do the fittings for 20 rooms cost, in J$, before GCT?
What is an emergency light called that is lit all the time, not only when the mains supply fails?
What is the smallest radius a cable may be bent to without damage called?
Which instrument measures how much light falls on a work surface?
Which hand tool is used to fix a lug or ferrule onto the end of a stranded conductor?
What is it called when two cable ends are connected together along a run, which should be avoided where possible?
What class of fitting is double insulated, so it has no protective conductor connection to its case?
What is the warmness or coolness of a lamp's light called, which is given in kelvin?
What is the maker's figure called for the greatest force with which a cable may be pulled?
What is the sensor called that switches a light on when it detects someone moving?
In which unit is the amount of light falling on a desk measured?

essays.stem: Describe how you would plan and coordinate a large cable pull through tray and conduit between the floors of a hotel.
essays.modelAnswer: I start with the cable schedule and drawings: the size and type of cable, its length, route and both ends. I check the maker's data for the maximum pulling force and minimum bending radius. I walk the route to check that tray and conduit are finished, clean and free of sharp edges, and I plan where the drum will stand, where rollers and corner sheaves are needed, and where people will be. I order the right drum length so there are no joints, and arrange delivery close to the day. I plan the crew: one person in charge, a drum handler, feeders at each floor and pullers, with radios or agreed signals so anyone can call a stop. I arrange the equipment: drum stands and spindle, pulling sock, rope or winch, rollers, lubricant and PPE. I agree the time with other trades, barrier the area, and brief the crew on hazards such as manual handling, pinch points and work at height. After the pull, the cable is labelled at both ends, sealed and checked for damage, and the length is recorded.
markingPoints: Uses the schedule, drawings and maker's limits (pulling force, bending radius)
Checks and prepares the route, drum position, rollers and sheaves
Plans crew roles and communication with one person in charge
Arranges equipment, timing with other trades, barriers and a safety briefing
Labels, seals, checks and records the cable after the pull

essays.stem: Explain how you would use a cable schedule and a luminaire (fixture) schedule to control the work and the materials on a project.
essays.modelAnswer: The cable schedule lists every cable with its reference, size, type, route, length and the two ends it connects. I use it to work out how much of each cable to order, to plan the order of the pulls, and to give the crew each day's cables. As each cable is pulled, labelled and terminated, I tick it off and record the actual length, so I can see progress and how much cable is left. The luminaire schedule lists each fitting by type, lamp, colour temperature, mounting and location. I use it to order the right number of each fitting, to check deliveries against it, and to issue fittings to each area. As fittings are installed and tested, I mark them off. The schedules show quickly what is done and what is left, so I can report progress honestly. Any change agreed with the client or designer is added to the schedules, with the date, so the final schedules match what was installed and can be given to the client at handover.
markingPoints: Describes what each schedule contains
Uses schedules for ordering and checking deliveries
Uses them to plan and issue daily work
Tracks progress by ticking off and recording actual lengths
Updates them with changes and hands them over as records

essays.stem: Describe how you would receive, store, protect and account for cable and fixtures on a building site, including security against theft.
essays.modelAnswer: When deliveries arrive, I check them against the order and the schedules: type, size, quantity and condition. I note any damage or shortage on the delivery note before signing, and report it to the supplier. Cable drums are rolled in the direction of the arrow and stored on firm, level ground or in a store, with the ends sealed. Fixtures are kept in their boxes in a dry, locked store, off the floor and away from where other trades are working, so they are not damaged or covered in dust. Copper cable is a target for thieves, so I arrange deliveries close to when it is needed, keep it locked away, and do not leave drums or offcuts lying around. I keep a stores record of what comes in, what is issued to each area and what is returned, so losses are noticed quickly. Installed fittings are covered while other trades work. At the end, leftover materials are returned and recorded, and scrap copper is recycled through the company, not sold privately.
markingPoints: Checks deliveries against order and schedules; records damage
Stores drums and fixtures correctly (dry, off the floor, ends sealed)
Security: deliveries close to need, locked store, nothing left lying around
Keeps a stores record of issues and returns
Protects installed fittings and deals properly with leftovers and scrap

essays.stem: Explain how you would coordinate the installation of light fittings in a suspended ceiling with the ceiling installer and other trades.
essays.modelAnswer: Before the ceiling goes in, I compare the lighting layout with the ceiling grid layout, the air-conditioning diffusers, sprinkler heads and smoke detectors, so fittings line up with the grid and do not clash. I raise any clashes at the coordination meeting and agree a combined ceiling plan. I make sure that all cables, boxes and supports for the fittings are in place before the grid is closed, with the drops left in the right place and long enough. I agree with the ceiling installer who cuts the holes for downlights, and the sizes from the maker's data. Heavy fittings are given their own hangers, not left to rest on the grid, unless the makers allow it. I check that fittings near insulation are rated for it. I agree the order of work so that fittings go in after the tiles are fitted and the dusty work is done, and they are covered if painting continues. Finally I make sure access panels are left where we need to reach junction boxes or drivers.
markingPoints: Compares layouts and resolves clashes with other services
Completes cables, boxes and supports before the ceiling closes
Agrees cut-outs and sizes with the ceiling installer
Supports heavy fittings properly and checks insulation contact
Agrees order of work, protection and access panels

essays.stem: Describe how to install a ceiling fan with a light kit safely and correctly, from choosing the support to the function test.
essays.modelAnswer: First I check the fan's weight and the maker's instructions, and make sure there is a fan-rated box or bracket fixed firmly to the structure, such as a beam or a brace between joists. An ordinary light box is not enough, because the fan's weight and shaking can pull it out. I check the blades will be at least the height the maker and specification require above the floor. I safely isolate the circuit: switch off, lock off, tag and prove dead with a tester checked before and after. I assemble the fan on the ground where possible. I hang it on the bracket using the safety cable or hook supplied, then connect line, neutral, protective conductor and the separate switched line for the light if there is one, using the right connectors, and fold the conductors neatly into the canopy. I fit the blades and balance them, and check all screws are tight. After the dead tests pass, a competent person energises the circuit and checks the speed control, the light, the direction switch and that the fan runs without wobbling.
markingPoints: Uses a fan-rated support fixed to the structure, with the reason
Checks the maker's instructions and blade height
Safe isolation with tester checked before and after
Correct hanging, connections and tidy conductors; blades fitted and balanced
Dead tests, then function test by a competent person

essays.stem: Explain what you would check when choosing and installing light fittings for outdoor and wet places in Jamaica, such as pool decks, car parks and bathrooms.
essays.modelAnswer: First I check the IP rating: fittings outdoors and in bathrooms must keep out rain, splashes and dust to the level the specification sets. Near pools and showers I check which zone the fitting is in, and that it is a type allowed there, often at extra-low voltage, and that the circuits have RCD protection. Near the sea, salt air corrodes metal, so I choose fittings with marine-grade finishes, stainless fixings and sealed glands. The strong sun can break down plastic, so outdoor plastic parts must be UV-resistant. For car parks and poles, I check that the bracket and pole are rated for hurricane winds. I make sure cable entries are sealed and face down where possible, so water does not run in, and that drain holes are left open where the maker requires. I use outdoor-rated cables and boxes, and photocells or timers to save energy. After installation, I check the seals are tight, and the fittings are tested dead, then function-tested by a competent person.
markingPoints: Checks IP rating for the location
Zones near pools and showers; RCD protection; extra-low voltage where needed
Corrosion-resistant and UV-resistant materials
Wind loading for poles and brackets
Sealed cable entries, outdoor-rated parts, testing

essays.stem: Describe the hazards of cable pulling and fixture installation on a large job, and the controls you would use.
essays.modelAnswer: Manual handling is a major hazard: drums, cables and fittings are heavy. We use drum stands, trolleys and winches, lift as a team and keep within safe weights. Pinch points at drums, rollers and pulling ropes can trap fingers, so we wear gloves, keep hands clear and have one person in charge who can call a stop. Work at height is needed for ceilings and high fittings, so we use mobile scaffolds or platform steps, not chairs or crates, and barrier off the area below to protect people from falling items. Electric shock is possible when connecting to existing circuits, so we always isolate, lock off, tag and prove dead with a tester checked before and after. Cutting and drilling produce dust and sharp edges, so we wear eye protection and masks and deburr ends. Glass and lamps can break, so we handle them with care and dispose of broken lamps safely. Heat in roof spaces can cause heat stress, so we plan breaks and drink water. Housekeeping keeps trip hazards away.
markingPoints: Manual handling: mechanical aids and team lifts
Pinch points: gloves, control of the pull, one person in charge
Work at height and falling objects: right access and barriers
Electric shock: safe isolation with tester checked before and after
Dust, sharp edges, broken glass, heat stress and housekeeping

essays.stem: Explain how you would supervise and check the quality of terminations and fixture installation done by a crew of four.
essays.modelAnswer: At the start I show the crew the standard I expect, using the specification and the makers' instructions, and I make a sample installation of each type of fitting and termination for them to copy. I give each person an area and the right tools, such as crimpers and a torque screwdriver. I check the first few items each person does: conductors stripped to the right length with no bare copper showing, no nicked strands, ferrules on stranded conductors where needed, terminals tight, protective conductors connected, cables labelled and neatly folded into boxes, and fittings level and firmly fixed. I correct problems straight away and explain why. After that I make regular spot checks, increasing them for anyone whose work had faults. I keep a simple quality checklist for each area, signed when the area passes. Faults found are written on a snag list and the person who did the work corrects them. I praise good work, and at the end of each day I note progress and quality issues in my report.
markingPoints: Sets the standard with specification, makers' instructions and a sample
Checks the first items of each person against clear points
Corrects problems promptly and explains why
Continues spot checks and uses a signed checklist
Records snags, has them corrected and reports progress

essays.stem: Describe the steps from finishing the fixtures on a project to handing over to the client: inspection, testing, snagging, documents and client briefing.
essays.modelAnswer: First I inspect every area against the drawings and schedules: all fittings and accessories are present, the right type, level, firmly fixed and clean, with labels and circuit charts complete. Then, with the circuits safely isolated, the crew carry out the dead tests: continuity of protective conductors, insulation resistance with lamps and drivers disconnected, and polarity. When these pass, a competent person energises the circuits and does the live tests and function tests: every switch, dimmer, sensor, photocell and emergency light works as designed. Any faults go on a snag list, which is worked through and checked again. I then prepare the documents: the certificate and test results, the updated cable and luminaire schedules, as-built drawings, and the makers' instructions and warranties. Finally I walk round with the client, show them how the controls, timers and emergency light test work, explain any maintenance, and get their signature on the handover sheet. Spare lamps and keys are handed over and recorded.
markingPoints: Final inspection against drawings and schedules
Dead tests, then live and function tests by a competent person
Snag list worked through and rechecked
Documents: certificate, results, schedules, as-builts, makers' information
Client briefing on controls and maintenance; signed handover

essays.stem: Explain how emergency lighting is installed and checked, and why fire-resistant cable and segregation are used for it.
essays.modelAnswer: Emergency lighting lets people find their way out safely when the normal lighting fails, for example in a power cut or a fire. Fittings are placed as the design shows: over exit doors, along escape routes, at changes of direction and level, and near fire-fighting equipment and first-aid points. Self-contained fittings have their own battery and are fed from the local lighting circuit, so they light if that circuit fails. The installer connects a permanent supply to charge the battery and, for maintained fittings, a switched supply as well. Fire-resistant cable is used where the design calls for it, so the circuit keeps working for a time during a fire. It is kept separate from other cables, so a fault or fire in an ordinary circuit does not damage it. After installation, a competent person checks that each fitting lights when its normal supply is cut and stays on for its rated time, and records the results. The client is shown how to do regular short tests and keep the log book.
markingPoints: Purpose of emergency lighting
Correct positions: exits, escape routes, changes of direction, equipment points
Correct connections, including the permanent charging supply
Fire-resistant cable and segregation, with reasons
Testing and recording by a competent person; client shown routine tests

practical1.title: Plan and lead a cable pull and termination to a cable schedule
practical1.brief: The assessor gives the group a training rig with a small distribution board, a conduit run with two bends and a draw-in box, a length of trunking and a cable tray leading to four accessory points, and a drawing of the circuits. The rig is NOT connected to any supply. As a group, prepare a cable schedule from the drawing: each cable's reference, size, type, route, length and ends. Plan the pull: where the drum stands go, where a roller is needed, who is drum handler, feeder, puller and leader, and the signals for start and stop. Set up the drum on its stands and spindle, fit the draw wire and pulling grip, and pull the cables in using lubricant where needed. Each member leads one pull. Label every cable at both ends, then terminate them at the board and the accessories. Check the terminations, then carry out dead tests (continuity of protective conductors and insulation resistance) and record the results. Tick off the schedule with the actual lengths used, and return and record the leftover cable.
materials: Training rig with board, conduit, trunking, tray and accessory boxes, not connected to any supply (from the assessor)
A small drum of cable, drum stands and spindle; draw wire or fish tape, pulling grip and cable lubricant
Corner roller or sheave, cable labels or markers
Hand tools, crimpers, ferrules and a torque screwdriver
Blank cable schedule and test record sheet
Gloves, safety glasses and platform steps
photos: The completed cable schedule before the pull
The drum set up on stands with the crew in their roles
A pull in progress, with the roller at the corner
Labels on both ends of a cable
Terminations at the board and at one accessory, close up
A dead test in progress and the test record
The schedule ticked off with actual lengths, and the leftover cable recorded
checklist: Helped write an accurate cable schedule
Led a pull with clear signals and kept the crew safe
Handled the drum and cable correctly without kinking or overbending it
Labelled cables at both ends to match the schedule
Made neat, tight terminations with no bare copper showing
Took part in the dead tests and recorded results correctly
Recorded actual lengths and leftover cable
safety: The rig is never connected to a supply during this task
Wear gloves and keep fingers clear of the drum, rollers and draw wire
Lift the drum with two people or a lifting aid
Use platform steps to reach high runs, never chairs or boxes
Warn others before each insulation test

practical2.title: Install and connect fixtures to a luminaire schedule
practical2.brief: The assessor gives the group a luminaire and fixture schedule and a training ceiling frame and wall with cables already in place, NOT connected to any supply. The schedule includes a ceiling fan on a fan-rated box, two recessed downlights in a suspended ceiling tile, an outdoor fitting with a photocell, a self-contained emergency light and a bathroom exhaust fan with a local isolator. As a group, first check the delivered fittings against the schedule and note any damage on the delivery sheet. Each member then leads the installation of one or two items, with the others helping and checking. Before connecting, isolate the frame's supply point, lock off with every member's padlock, tag and prove dead with a tester checked before and after. Fix each item level and firmly, as the maker's instructions say, and connect it neatly. Inspect the work against the schedule and a checklist, and carry out dead tests. The assessor then energises the frame and the group watches the function test of every item, including the emergency light when its supply is cut. Write a snag list, put the snags right with the frame isolated again, and prepare a short handover pack.
materials: Training ceiling frame and wall with cables in place, not connected to any supply
Ceiling fan and fan-rated box or bracket; two recessed downlights and a ceiling tile
Outdoor IP-rated fitting with photocell; self-contained emergency light; exhaust fan with isolator
Luminaire and fixture schedule, delivery sheet, inspection checklist, snag list and handover sheet
Two-pole tester and proving unit; insulation and continuity tester
Lock-off kit, padlocks and tags; hand tools, connectors and platform steps
photos: The delivered fittings checked against the schedule
The supply point locked off and the tester being checked
The fan-rated box fixed to the frame before the fan is hung
Each item installed, with its connections before the cover goes on
The emergency light lit when its supply is cut during the assessor's test
The completed checklist, snag list and handover pack
checklist: Checked fittings against the schedule and recorded any damage
Isolated, locked off and proved dead correctly, with the tester checked before and after
